newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to open steel talks with Russia.
newsitem.headline: EU to open steel talks with Russia.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it had been authorised to negotiate new five-year steel trade accords with Russia, Ukraine and Kazakhstan.

The talks, which will aim to progressively open up the European Union market to steel products from the three countries from 1997 to 2001, have been approved by EU governments, the Commission said in a statement.
Under present arrangements, certain categories of flat and long steel products exported from Russia, Ukraine and Kazakhstan to the EU are subject to quotas.
"In 1996, these limits amount to one million tonnes," the Commission said.
The limits would be relaxed under the new accords in line with steps taken by the three countries to apply certain competition, state aid and environmental protection rules.
The Commission said the three countries exported to the EU about 7.2 million tonnes of steel and other ferrous products with a value of 1.7 billion Ecus ($2 billion) in 1995.
By contrast, the EU exported to them about 175,000 tonnes with a value of about 104 million Ecus ($130 million), it said.

Exports from the three countries that were subject to EU quotas represented less than 12 percent of their total steel exports to the Union in both volume and value terms, it said. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
